title: Principles of Metareasoning
authors: Russell, S.; Wefald, E.
training_target_description: analytic expected value of computation (not learned from paired outcomes)
inference_decision_description: execute a computation only if its expected improvement in decision quality exceeds its cost
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: defines 'value of computation' = expected benefit of a computation minus its cost, decided BEFORE the computation
important_difference: no segmentation, no learned predictor, no paired GT-derived gain target; analytic/decision-theoretic
notes: Conceptual ancestor of the entire framing. Our pre-refinement gate is an instance of value-of-computation. Must be cited; blocks any claim of algorithmic novelty for the gate idea itself.

title: Adaptive Inference: Theoretical Limits and Unexplored Opportunities
authors: Hor, S.; Qian, Y.; Pilanci, M.; Arbabian, A.
training_target_description: theoretical bounds on achievable efficiency/performance gain of adaptive inference
inference_decision_description: framework-level: how much gain is available if inference adapts to input
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: formalises the 'performance-preserving efficiency gain' objective we target
important_difference: theory/bounds only; no learned benefit predictor, no medical segmentation, no gate implementation
notes: Provides the theoretical framing for 'no performance penalty + efficiency gain'. Supports, does not occupy, our specific mechanism.

title: Cascaded Classifier for Pareto-Optimal Accuracy-Cost Trade-Off Using off-the-Shelf ANNs
authors: Latotzke, C.; Loh, J.; Gemmeke, T.
training_target_description: optimal pass-on criteria derived from per-stage accuracy/cost statistics (not a learned per-sample gain)
inference_decision_description: decide whether to pass a sample to the next, more expensive cascade stage BEFORE running it
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: EXECUTE-vs-SKIP decision before the expensive stage; explicit cost term; class of optimal pass-on criteria
important_difference: classification not segmentation; criterion from score statistics rather than a paired GT-derived ΔQ regression; no fallback; no multi-domain
notes: Mechanically the closest non-medical gate. Our differentiator is the learned ΔQ target for a SEGMENTATION refinement, not the gate concept.

title: Rapid Object Detection Using a Boosted Cascade of Simple Features
authors: Viola, P.; Jones, M.
training_target_description: boosted weak classifiers; early stages reject easy negatives
inference_decision_description: cheap stages gate expensive stages; reject early, escalate on uncertainty
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: canonical cheap-gates-expensive architecture with early rejection and escalation
important_difference: detection, hand-designed cascade, decisions from classifier scores not a learned ΔQ benefit
notes: The canonical antecedent for 'cheap gate before expensive stage'. Establishes the general idea decades before our work.

title: Metalearners for Estimating Heterogeneous Treatment Effects Using Machine Learning
authors: Kunzel, S. R.; Sekhon, J. S.; Bickel, P. J.; Yu, B.
training_target_description: CATE tau(x)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)|x]; S/T/X-learners estimate the paired difference of outcomes across two conditions
inference_decision_description: estimate per-unit treatment effect to target a treatment regime
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: EXACT formal structure of our target: a paired difference of outcomes under two conditions, estimated per unit before deciding
important_difference: no image/segmentation, no execution cost term, no gate on a compute action; the 'treatment' is a policy, not a refinement pass
notes: Our DeltaQ = Q(refined)-Q(global) is a T-learner/X-learner instantiation of CATE. This constrains any claim that the TARGET FORMULATION is novel; the paired-gain target is standard causal-inference machinery.

title: Consistent Estimators for Learning to Defer to an Expert
authors: Mozannar, H.; Sontag, D.
training_target_description: Bayes-consistent surrogate losses for the joint predictor+deferral decision, calibrated to the expert's cost
inference_decision_description: predict yourself, or defer to a costlier expert, decided before accepting the output
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: learned pre-action deferral with an explicit cost asymmetry and a preservation/fallback structure
important_difference: classification with a human/specialist expert; deferral target is not a GT-derived Dice gain; no segmentation, no multi-domain
notes: Establishes 'learned when to escalate to the expensive path, with cost' as a solved general problem.

title: Judging from Support-set: A New Way to Utilize Few-Shot Segmentation for Segmentation Refinement Process
authors: Moon, S.; Liu, Q. (T.); Kong, H.; Khan, M. H.
training_target_description: no training: a few-shot (SegGPT) support-set IoU delta decides whether the refined mask beats the coarse mask
inference_decision_description: POST-HOC: refinement is run FIRST, then JFS judges success and may revert to the coarse mask
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: SAME problem framing ('was the refinement worth it?') and a paired coarse-vs-refined quality comparison with revert-on-failure fallback
important_difference: DECIDES AFTER refinement (post-hoc verifier), so it saves NO compute; no learned predictor; no cost term; no multi-domain; no medical; decision under test
notes: THE single closest functional analogue in segmentation. Our margin depends entirely on the pre-execution property and the learned GT-derived ΔQ regression. Must be the headline comparison.

title: Med-DANet V2: A Flexible Dynamic Architecture for Efficient Medical Volumetric Segmentation
authors: Shen, H.; Zhang, Y.; Wang, W.; Chen, C.; Liu, J.; Song, S.; Li, J.
training_target_description: Decision Network + Crop Position Network learn a policy to pick a foreground region and a stage-wise quantization level per slice (difficulty/efficiency proxy), NOT a paired GT-derived gain
inference_decision_description: BEFORE segmenting each slice, select the foreground crop and quantization level; resource budget informs the choice
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: medical, slice-adaptive, decides per-sample how much compute to spend BEFORE running the segmentation model, with an explicit efficiency objective
important_difference: selects a REGION + bit-width, not whether to run a refinement vs skip it; no paired ΔQ target; no fallback of a preserved output; single modality-domain
notes: Strongest medical precedent for 'decide compute allocation before running the model'. Our differentiator: the decision target is the expected Dice GAIN of an optional refinement, not a crop/quantization policy.

title: Med-DANet: Dynamic Architecture Network for Efficient Medical Volumetric Segmentation
authors: Shen, H.; Zhang, Y.; Wang, W.; Chen, C.; Liu, J.; Song, S.; Li, J.
training_target_description: a decision network selects a suitable 2D candidate model from a model bank per slice, supervised by a difficulty/efficiency objective
inference_decision_description: per-slice model selection BEFORE running the expensive model; cost-efficiency trade-off
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: pioneering dynamic-architecture decision for medical segmentation with a cost/accuracy trade-off
important_difference: chooses among models, not whether to refine; target is difficulty/efficiency, not a paired Dice gain; no fallback
notes: Predecessor of Med-DANet V2. Together they occupy 'dynamic decision + medical + efficiency'.

title: Adaptive Patching for High-resolution Image Segmentation with Transformers
authors: Zhang, E.; Lyngaas, I.; Chen, Q.; Wang, X.; Igarashi, K.; Huo, Z.; Wahib, M.; Munetomo, M.
training_target_description: no learned gain: patches are selected by local image-detail heuristics before attention
inference_decision_description: BEFORE attention, choose which patches to feed the transformer based on image detail
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: medical, high-resolution, decides BEFORE expensive attention where to spend compute; adaptive computation on a spatial grid
important_difference: selection heuristic is detail-based, not a learned ΔQ benefit; no execute/skip on a refinement OUTPUT; no fallback; single domain
notes: Shows pre-computation spatial compute allocation is established in medical CV. Our target (paired Dice gain regression) is the differentiator.

title: SegRefiner: Towards Model-Agnostic Segmentation Refinement with Discrete Diffusion Process
authors: Wang, M.; Ding, H.; Wang, M.; et al.
training_target_description: discrete diffusion denoising of a coarse mask toward target boundaries
inference_decision_description: always refine; no decision, no gate
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: represents the unconditional expensive refinement that our gate would decide on (the primitive, not the gate)
important_difference: no benefit prediction, no gate, no cost, no fallback; it IS the refinement we would gate
notes: Cited as the refinement primitive family. Confirms that refinement itself is not novel.

title: Soft Dice Confidence: A Near-Optimal Confidence Estimator for Selective Prediction in Semantic Segmentation
authors: Borges, B. L. C.; Pacheco, B. M.; Silva, D.
training_target_description: near-optimal confidence estimator for the Dice of the CURRENT prediction, from marginal posteriors
inference_decision_description: image-level abstention when confidence is low (selective prediction)
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: GT-free estimate of segmentation quality with an abstention decision, validated across six medical tasks including OOD
important_difference: estimates the quality of the CURRENT mask, never the benefit of a future refinement; no expensive action; no cost; abstains rather than routing
notes: Establishes GT-free quality estimation as solved. Our predictor must be the GAIN of an action, not the current quality — this paper is the boundary that separates the two.

title: Real-time Prediction of Segmentation Quality
authors: Laves, M.-H.; Ihler, S.; Ortmaier, T.
medical_domains: (medical; cite record verified at conference level)
training_target_description: regression of CURRENT segmentation quality (e.g. Dice) from network features
inference_decision_description: report predicted quality; no routing action
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: the classic precursor: predict segmentation quality directly
important_difference: predicts CURRENT quality, not the gain of an optional refinement; no action, no cost, no fallback
notes: Cited as the origin of the 'predict quality' line that our work must explicitly separate from 'predict benefit of action'.

title: Towards Ground-truth-free Evaluation of Any Segmentation in Medical Images
authors: Huang, S.; et al. (EvanySeg)
training_target_description: learns to assess the quality of ANY given segmentation without ground truth, across modalities
inference_decision_description: score an existing segmentation; no routing/action
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: GT-free, multi-modality, universal quality assessment — the input machinery our benefit predictor would need
important_difference: scores quality, does not predict the DELTA of a future refinement; no action, no cost, no fallback
notes: Shows a universal GT-free evaluator is feasible; reinforces that our controllable novelty is the ACTION-BENEFIT target, not GT-free evaluation.

title: Learning to Abstain: Reliable Medical Image Segmentation With Rejection Option
authors: Sanisoglu, N.; Navab, N.; Kim, S. T.
training_target_description: an extra (M+1)-th reject channel trained to flag uncertain pixels in real time
inference_decision_description: abstain from labelling uncertain pixels; report Dice at target coverage
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: a rejection/abstention mechanism that preserves reliability, with a coverage-level reliability metric
important_difference: abstains on CURRENT pixel uncertainty; there is no expensive action to gate, no paired gain, no cost; the 'reject' is over pixels not over a refinement outcome
notes: The nearest 'reject to preserve reliability' rule; will be cited against any strong fallback claim. Different because rejection targets pixels, not a computed candidate refinement.

title: Conformal 3D Lesion Segmentation with Balanced Risk Control
authors: Tan, B.; et al. (CLS)
training_target_description: distribution-free conformal calibration of segmentation thresholds for balanced risk control across five backbones
inference_decision_description: set thresholds so a risk target is met; no action routing
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: distribution-free risk control on segmentation — the tool a 'certified' guarantee would need
important_difference: controls risk of a single output; does not predict or bound the GAIN of a future refinement; no action, no cost, no fallback
notes: Central to the certification-terminology audit: it defines what 'risk-controlled' can defensibly mean. We cannot inherit conformal guarantees for a counterfactual gain without constructing them.

title: UniverSeg: Universal Medical Image Segmentation
authors: Butoi, V. I.; Gonzalez Ortiz, J. J.; Ma, T.; Sabuncu, M. R.; Guttag, J.; Dalca, A. V.
training_target_description: single frozen model conditioned on a support set of image-label pairs via CrossBlock
inference_decision_description: no decision: one forward pass, no routing
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: a single frozen model spanning many medical domains — the 'shared multi-domain' pillar of our framing
important_difference: no refinement, no gate, no cost, no benefit prediction; conditioning is by support set, not FiLM
notes: Removes 'shared multi-domain medical segmentor' as a novel component.

title: Segment Anything in Medical Images
authors: Ma, J.; He, Y.; Li, F.; Han, L.; et al.
medical_domains: CT, MRI, endoscopy, dermoscopy, US, X-ray, mammography, fundus (11 modalities)
training_target_description: SAM fine-tuned on 1.5M+ medical image-mask pairs with box prompts
inference_decision_description: prompt-conditioned single forward pass
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: universal multi-modality medical segmentation via prompting
important_difference: no refinement/rejection, no routing, no benefit prediction, no resource objective
notes: Further removes 'shared multi-domain/universal medical segmentation' from novelty.

title: M4oE: A Foundation Model for Medical Multimodal Image Segmentation with Mixture of Experts
authors: Jiang, Y.; Shen, Y.
training_target_description: modality-specific experts with a gating network that modulates each expert's contribution; gates trained during fine-tuning
inference_decision_description: route each input to/blend experts per modality; no execute/skip on a refinement
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: multi-domain + learned MoE routing in one medical model with an efficiency claim
important_difference: routing selects EXPERTS (a pathway), not whether to run an optional refinement; no paired gain target, no fallback
notes: Occupies 'multi-domain + learned routing' in medical segmentation. Forces our routing novelty to be about the DECISION TARGET, not the routing mechanism.

title: DeferredSeg: A Multi-Expert Deferral Framework for Medical Image Segmentation
authors: Tian, Z.; Sun, Y.; Wang, Y.; Shi, Y.; Yin, Y.
training_target_description: pixel-wise surrogate collaboration loss supervises an aggregated deferral predictor; spatial-coherence loss; load-balancing penalty
inference_decision_description: BEFORE finalising, route each pixel to the base segmentor or a human expert
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: predict-then-route over a second pathway in dense medical segmentation, with a preservation structure
important_difference: the second pathway is a HUMAN EXPERT, not an optional automated refinement; no learned GT-derived ΔQ regression; no cost/resource term; not multi-domain
notes: The closest 'predict-then-decide over a second pathway' in dense medical segmentation. Our differentiators: the action is an AUTOMATED refinement, the target is a paired GT-derived Dice gain, and cost is explicit.

title: Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
authors: Graves, A.
training_target_description: per-step halting probability trained with a ponder-cost penalty on the number of steps
inference_decision_description: decide online how many computation steps to take before emitting an output
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: learned, differentiable allocation of computation with an explicit cost penalty
important_difference: decides online during compute, not by predicting the GAIN of a distinct future block; no segmentation; no paired ΔQ
notes: Canonical 'learned halting with cost'. Our pre-execution gain prediction is a stricter variant but the family is well occupied.

title: SkipNet: Learning Dynamic Routing in Convolutional Networks
authors: Wang, X.; Yu, F.; Dou, Z.-Y.; Darrell, T.; Gonzalez, J. E.
training_target_description: gated residual layers with a hybrid supervised+RL objective; harder inputs use more layers
inference_decision_description: per-input, per-layer decision to compute or skip a residual block
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: learned per-input skip/execute of computation with a resource benefit
important_difference: skips internal blocks of one network, not an optional external refinement stage; no paired quality gain; no medical
notes: Establishes learned per-input execute/skip of computation. Our 'skip' is coarser (an entire refinement stage) and target-supervised.

title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically Allocating Compute in Transformer-Based Language Models
authors: Raposo, D.; Ritter, S.; Richards, B.; Lillicrap, T.; Humphreys, P. C.; Santoro, A.
training_target_description: per-token router learns top-k compute allocation through a block vs a residual skip
inference_decision_description: route a token around a block or through it
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: learned per-input compute allocation (through vs around)
important_difference: internal block routing in an LLM; not a distinct refinement stage; no quality-gain target; no medical
notes: Context for the conditional-compute family; not medical and not gain-targeted.

title: Faster Segment Anything: Towards Lightweight SAM for Mobile Applications (MobileSAM)
authors: Zhang, C.; Han, D.; Qiao, Y.; Kim, J. U.; Bae, S.-H.; Lee, S.; Hong, C. S.
training_target_description: decoupled distillation of SAM's ViT-H image encoder into a tiny ViT
inference_decision_description: single lightweight forward pass; no routing
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: mobile/CPU deployment as an explicit design objective for segmentation
important_difference: compression only; no benefit prediction, no gate, no fallback; engineering not algorithmic novelty
notes: Shows device-aware segmentation is crowded; supports classifying device-awareness as ENGINEERING VALUE unless integrated with the benefit gate.

title: nnU-Net: a self-configuring method for deep learning-based biomedical image segmentation
authors: Isensee, F.; Jaeger, P. F.; Kohl, S. A. A.; Petersen, J.; Maier-Hein, K. H.
training_target_description: three-stage 3D cascade: coarse low-resolution segmentation then full-resolution refinement; plus a region-based trainer that samples patches around hard/foreground voxels
inference_decision_description: the cascade second stage ALWAYS runs; no gate, no skip
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: coarse-to-fine medical refinement with a hard-region patch trainer — the always-execute baseline our gate improves on
important_difference: refinement is unconditional (always runs); no benefit prediction, no gate, no fallback, no cost-aware decision
notes: The canonical always-run cascade. Our work is explicitly the conditional version of this; we must position against it, not claim the cascade as novel.

title: From single to universal: tiny lesion detection in medical imaging
authors: Chou, P.-H.; et al.
training_target_description: survey of multi-scale, attention, super-resolution, patch/zoom strategies for tiny lesions
inference_decision_description: n/a (survey)
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: systematic treatment of tiny-lesion strategies including zoom/refinement and 'universal' framing
important_difference: a survey; no gate, no benefit predictor, no cost; confirms the tiny-object problem and the zoom primitive are established
notes: Precludes any novelty claim resting on 'tiny objects' or 'zoom refinement of tiny structures' alone.

title: Learning to Focus and Precise Cropping: A Reinforcement Learning Framework with Information Gaps and Grounding Loss for MLLMs
authors: Zhao, X.; Tan, Z.; Sheng, D.; Chen, T.; Liu, Y.; Wu, Y.; Gong, T.; Chu, Q.; Yu, N.
training_target_description: two-stage RL (no trajectory supervision): an 'Information Gap' mechanism trains the model to answer by focusing on cropped regions, 'driven by the information gain these regions provide'
inference_decision_description: learn (via RL reward) where to crop / how much detail is worth attending to
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: the closest general-CV analogue of 'act on the region that provides the most GAIN' — it optimises a gain signal for a regional action
important_difference: VQA/cropping, not segmentation; the gain is an implicit RL reward, NOT a supervised paired Q(refined)-Q(global) regression; no fallback; no cost term
notes: Directly threatens the uniqueness of 'learn the benefit of a regional action'. Our defence: explicit, supervised, GT-derived ΔQ regression used as a PRE-EXECUTION gate for a segmentation refinement.

title: Scale-aware Super-resolution Network with Dual Affinity learning for lesion segmentation
authors: (arXiv:2305.19063, scale-aware SR for lesions)
training_target_description: dual-path network that super-resolves the lesion mask AND the lesion image inside the region
inference_decision_description: region refinement applied unconditionally
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: regional zoom/refinement targeted at small lesions — the refinement primitive for tiny structures
important_difference: no gate, no benefit prediction, no cost; refinement always applied
notes: Confirms 'zoom/refine regions for tiny structures' is prior art; our novelty must be the CONDITIONAL application.

title: On Optimum Recognition Error and Reject Tradeoff
authors: Chow, C. K.
training_target_description: optimal reject rule from the posterior distribution (analytical)
inference_decision_description: accept a decision or reject it, based on posterior; the theoretical basis of the reject option
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: foundational formulation of the accept/reject decision as a trade-off
important_difference: no learning of a future action's gain; single decision, no second computation to gate
notes: Historical antecedent of the reject/fallback idea; included for completeness, not a competitive threat.

title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
authors: Ren, S.; He, K.; Girshick, R.; Sun, J.
training_target_description: region proposal network predicts objectness scores and box offsets; proposals gate the expensive per-region head
inference_decision_description: cheap proposals decide WHICH regions receive the expensive classification/regression
closest_similarity_to_our_candidate: a cheap upstream network decides whether an expensive downstream computation is worth running, per region
important_difference: detection; objectness is a proxy for 'has an object', not the GAIN of a refinement; the expensive head still always runs on selected regions
notes: Well-known precedent for 'cheap predictor gates expensive computation per region'. Reinforces that the gate concept is not novel; the ΔQ TARGET is the defensible part.
